editions.text:
The station recorded 90 feeder visits, a sharp drop from the seven-day average of 200.1. While the species count of 17 sat slightly above the weekly mean of 16.9, the visual traffic was sparse compared to the recent high-activity days. Regulars like the Carolina Wren and Tufted Titmouse remained consistent, holding steady counts that align with their presence every day this week.

Acoustic activity stayed above the previous average, with 17 species detected. The absence of Mourning Doves marked the first break in their seven-day streak. This quiet day follows the period after the new audio source was installed on September 13, which has stabilized detection records since the switch from the older microphone.

The day featured 8 confirmed visual visits, a fraction of the typical volume. No new species were recorded for the first time at this station. The final visual record came from a Carolina Wren, logged one minute after sunset.

The first light on the tube feeder belonged to a Brown-headed Cowbird, a confident visit logged thirteen minutes before sunrise at this station. As the sun rose, the Carolina Wren began its vocal shift, dominating the morning air with a heavy acoustic presence that far outpaced the recent seven-day average. By eight o’clock, the feeder traffic had surged, with Tufted Titmice and Carolina Chickadees moving steadily through the mix.

This morning is noticeably busier than the same time on recent days, with total visits already exceeding the average by nearly a third. The visual record remains strong despite a quieter vocal chorus than usual, punctuated by a solitary Rose-breasted Grosbeak and a likely Orchard Oriole.
